verdict.rationale: Plausible's own docs list a 'User journeys' feature for exploring the paths visitors take. The site says you can 'explore the paths visitors actually take to discover flows you didn't predict.' This is a first-party path-exploration capability, but the evidence is only short listing-level mentions. Older community comments (comm-5, comm-6) say Plausible lacked user-flow tracking; they appear to predate this feature and do not concretely show it fails, so they lower confidence rather than creating a dispute. Missing for 10: documentation that paths can be anchored before or after a chosen key event or goal, detail on how deep the path exploration goes, and independent hands-on corroboration that user journeys work.

support.subject: As a product-manager, I can explore the paths users actually take before or after a key event
